s: spirit (mental disposition, ethos, especially one shared among a group; energy, enthousiasm)
Wir haben einen sehr guten Spirit in der Mannschaft.
We have a great spirit among the team.
Ich fühle total den Spirit von all seinen Liedern.
I totally feel the energy of all his songs.
Spirit.et: Late 20th century, borrowed from English spirit. Doublet of Esprit, Spiritus, and Sprit.

Spiritus lenis.et: Borrowed from Latin spīritus lēnis (“smooth breath”).

Spiritus asper.et: Borrowed from Latin spīritus asper (“rough breath”).

s: breathing; a glottal consonant, usually /h/; a (diacritical) mark for its presence or absence
Spiritus.et: 15th century, borrowed from Latin spiritus. Doublet of Esprit, Spirit, and Sprit.

s: scrawny, thin, weakly (especially of plants and people)
[Der Hengst] war auf der Flachen nicht an den Start zu bringen, so wenig wie jetzt an die Hürde. Dabei könnte er durch die spirrelige Hecke einfach durchlaufen.
[The stallion] was impossible to get going across flat ground, just as little as with the hurdles now. When, really, it could just walk right on through the thin brush.
Als wir gerade drei Bier bestellen wollen, steht hinter mir ein spirreliges Männchen mit breitem Grinsen.
Just as we're about to order three beers, a scrawny little man with a wide grin ends up standing behind us.
spirrelig.et: Potentially related to Spier (“(point of a) budding reed, stalk”).
